clue.text: Intrudes in health resort, breaking locks

indicators.note: breaking says the resort word forces its way into the middle of the hair word

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: A burglar gets into a wellness retreat by smashing the padlocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts the resort inside the hair; 'in' merely links definition to wordplay. The locks look like door fastenings but are hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who enters land without permission intrudes on it.

clue.text: Spain's premier vintage snapped up at auction?

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of the country's name is taken

parts.note: vintage as an adjective means old

explanation.surface: A top Spanish wine is bought eagerly by bidders at a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premier' looks like a prime minister or a top wine, but only picks the first letter of Spain's.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a lot knocked down to a bidder has been bought, the auctioneer's cry on the hammer falling.

clue.text: Shock about soldiers finding gear

indicators.note: about says the shock word goes around the soldiers

parts.note: to shock is to appal
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: People are alarmed that troops have come across some equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'finding' only links to the definition. The soldiers are the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; gear here is clothing rather than kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are informal or formal words for clothing.

clue.text: Trouble encountered by prophet going round part of Africa

indicators.note: going round turns the whole run of trouble plus prophet back to front

parts.note: to trouble someone is to ail them
Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A seer travelling around a region of Africa runs into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns the trouble and the prophet together as one run, so the prophet's letters come out first. 'encountered by' only sets the two side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a country in the Horn of the continent.

clue.text: Bartender's outside with the sign's flashing light

indicators.note: outside takes the first and last letters of the bartender word, ignoring the possessive
something flashing changes rapidly, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The barman stands out front with the pub's blinking neon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flashing light' reads as one phrase but splits: 'flashing' is the anagram signal and the last word alone is the definition. 'outside' ignores the possessive on Bartender's.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: luminosity, the quality of giving off illumination.

clue.text: Endless row about the love of football?

indicators.note: about turns the shortened word to face the other way
endless says the row word loses its final letter

parts.note: a row of things is a line
the last letter of the row word, which endless removes

explanation.surface: A never-ending argument over people's passion for the beautiful game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts LINE to LIN and 'about' turns it round. Love is tennis's word for zero; football's word for the same score is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivalent: tennis says love for a score of zero where British football results say this, as in two–zero.

clue.text: Invest in road repairs

indicators.note: repairs means the letters of the two words before it are put right in a new order

explanation.surface: Put money into mending the highways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repairs' rearranges IN ROAD. Invest is not financial here: it means to install someone formally in office, as with a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the ceremonial sense: to confer holy orders or office on someone.

clue.text: Faint lights not seen during this

definitions.meaning: a faint is a temporary loss of consciousness
a power cut or wartime precaution when everything goes dark

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers a swoon and a period when all illumination is cut or hidden.

clue.text: Autocratic sort reversed Scotland Yard corruption?

indicators.note: reversed says the whimsical phrase is written back to front

parts.note: Scotland Yard houses the CID, London's detective branch, so corruption there is whimsically 'rot at CID'

explanation.surface: A tyrant cleans up bent coppers at police headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the Metropolitan Police headquarters, home of the CID (Criminal Investigation Department). Corruption there is 'rot at CID', and 'reversed' writes that whole phrase backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a ruler with absolute, unchecked power.

clue.text: Dress not half revolutionary? It's old hat

indicators.note: not half says only the first half of the dress word is kept

parts.note: to dress someone is to clothe them
Che Guevara is crossword's stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: A frock that is hardly radical: frankly, it is passé.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps CLO from CLOTHE; Che Guevara follows. 'Old hat' usually means outdated, but here it is literally a hat of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bell-shaped women's headpiece fashionable in the 1920s.

clue.text: Test pilot's speed, quietly taking off

indicators.note: taking off says the quiet letter leaves the speed word

parts.note: speed is pace
P is piano, the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: An experimental aircraft's velocity as it silently leaves the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' removes P from PACE. The surface makes it an aircraft leaving the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a crack flyer, the sort trusted to try out new aircraft.

clue.text: Questioning validity of John Wesley's admission right away

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is removed from the admission

parts.note: Wesley, founder of Methodism, was a famous preacher, so he might admit 'I'm preaching'

explanation.surface: Doubting whether the Methodist founder's confession holds up, immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: John Wesley founded Methodism and preached constantly, so his admission is I'M PREACHING; 'away' drops the R. 'right away' looks like 'immediately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to challenge the credibility of testimony or a witness.

clue.text: Dishing out punishments

indicators.note: out means the letters of the word before it are disturbed from their order

explanation.surface: Handing down penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DISHING. 'Dishing out' reads as one phrasal verb but splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: beatings or thrashings given as correction.

clue.text: Band ordered to include fiddle

indicators.note: to include says the ordered word takes the fiddle word inside it

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered
to fiddle is to rig, to manipulate dishonestly

explanation.surface: A musical group is told to bring in a violinist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' is the container signal. Neither Band nor fiddle is musical here: one is a body of people, the other a swindle, and 'ordered' is an old past tense of bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an organised group of people, such as a military unit.

clue.text: Close to target with weapon

parts.note: an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A marksman nearing the bullseye, gun in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is not a link here but gives the letter W. The definition is the hint given in a guessing game.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: in hiding or guessing games, a seeker nearing the answer is told they are getting this.

clue.text: His Eminence trapped in quarry in time gone by

indicators.note: trapped in says the two pieces are caught inside the quarry word

parts.note: quarry is hunted prey
taken as written
an eminence is a hill, and a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A cardinal got stuck in a stone pit long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped in' is the container signal. 'His Eminence' looks like a cardinal's title but splits into two pieces, the second a hill; the quarry is hunted, not dug.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the ages before written records.

clue.text: Players like a sauna after stripping

indicators.note: stripping removes the outside, so the sauna-like word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a sauna is steamy
first letter of the sauna-like word, stripped off
last letter of the sauna-like word, stripped off

explanation.surface: Footballers enjoy the hot room once they have undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after stripping' takes the first and last letters off STEAMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a side, the group who play together.

clue.text: Windows version stocked in Ireland? Daughter bought it

indicators.note: stocked in says the software name is held inside the country's name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
XP is a version of Microsoft Windows
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A shop in Ireland carries some old software and a girl purchases it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocked in' is the container signal, and the Irish name for the country is needed. 'Bought it' is no purchase: it is slang for died.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: to have 'bought it' is to have died.

clue.text: For instance, rain regularly interrupts a country ramble?

indicators.note: interrupts says these pieces break into the run of the others

parts.note: a means per, as in ten pounds a head
a country is a nation

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the weather word

explanation.surface: Showers, say, keep spoiling a walk in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupts' is the container signal and 'regularly' picks alternate letters of rain. The sneaky piece is the small 'a', used as in 'ten pounds a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a wandering journey, especially a long one on foot.

clue.text: Welcome Salvation Army music maker

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Greet a brass-band player from the Sally Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to greet or acknowledge someone with respect.

clue.text: Wind blowing later? Yes

indicators.note: blowing scatters things about, so the letters of the two following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Will it be gusty this afternoon? It will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing' rearranges LATER YES. It reads as part of the weather forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an air current named for the compass point it comes from.

clue.text: Here Disney World spectacles cover surface of reclaimed ground

indicators.note: cover says the spectacles go around the other pieces

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacles

indicators.note: the surface is the top, so the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: ground is land

explanation.surface: The theme park's shows occupy the top of drained swampland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' is the container signal, with the spectacles drawn as two round letters, and 'surface of' picks a first letter. The resort really was built on drained Florida swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Location: the Florida city where the resort stands.

clue.text: Useless correspondence guided bankrupt person, as Spooner might have said

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words

parts.note: guided means led
a bankrupt is a debtor, someone who owes money

explanation.surface: Pointless mail steered an insolvent man, or so the muddled don put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of LED DEBTOR and it is heard as the answer; the swap works by sound, not spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: mail that cannot be delivered or returned; also a law no longer enforced.

clue.text: So nearly everyone entertained by great tunes in party entertainment

indicators.note: entertained by says the first pieces are taken in as guests by the later ones

parts.note: great means much, as in great or much rejoicing
sic is Latin for so or thus

indicators.note: nearly says the everyone word falls one letter short

parts.note: everyone is all
the final letter that nearly removes
airs are tunes

explanation.surface: Almost all the guests enjoy the fine songs played at the do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' is the container signal and 'nearly' shortens the word for everyone. 'So' is the Latin word editors use; the second 'in' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a children's game of circling seats until the melody stops.

clue.text: Broadcaster once turned up sound of trumpet accompanying comic briefly

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the whole run is read from bottom to top
accompanying sets the trumpet noise beside the comic word

parts.note: wah-wah is the wavering noise of a muted trumpet

indicators.note: briefly says the comic word loses its last letter

parts.note: comic as an adjective means droll
the last letter that briefly cuts off

explanation.surface: A veteran radio presenter arrives to a fanfare with a comedian in tow, for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts DROLL to DROL; 'turned up' reads WAHWAH DROL upwards. The answer is the nickname of William Joyce, who broadcast Nazi propaganda to Britain in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the nickname of a wartime propaganda radio voice.

clue.text: Business magazine's No 1 puzzle setter

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: No 1 means the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: The top crossword compiler at a trade journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 1' takes M from magazine's. 'puzzle setter' reads as one job but the puzzle is wordplay; the setter is one who sets words to music.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: one who sets words to music, or the term for a crossword compiler.

clue.text: Lunched, daringly consuming cheese

indicators.note: consuming says the two words have swallowed the answer within their run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone had a midday meal and boldly ate dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' shows the answer sits across the join of 'Lunched' and 'daringly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hard English variety named after a Somerset village.

clue.text: A little money dispatched by Aussie PM, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: dispatched is sent, and Australians call the afternoon (pm) the arvo: 'sent arvo'

explanation.surface: A small sum is said to have been wired by Australia's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is not a Prime Minister but the afternoon, which Australians call the 'arvo'. SENT ARVO, heard, gives the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small coin, a hundredth of a peso or similar unit.

clue.text: Citadel ready to house British army leader

indicators.note: to house says the money word gives room inside to the other letters

parts.note: ready, or readies, is British slang for cash

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A fortress is prepared to quarter a UK general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to house' puts B and A ('leader' of army) inside CASH. 'Ready' is British slang for cash in hand, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the fortress of a North African city.

clue.text: Jolly place to eat after abandoning car

indicators.note: after abandoning says the vehicle is dropped from the eating place

parts.note: a carvery is a British restaurant serving roast meat carved to order
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheerful spot for dinner once you have ditched the motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after abandoning' is the deletion signal; the place to eat is a British roast-meat restaurant. Jolly is an adverb here, as in 'jolly good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an intensifier: British 'jolly good' means extremely good.
